title: I tested FLUX 3 at editing real videos, from changing my outfit and a...

The good: it’s fast and cheap, at $0.03 per second of generated video in 720p. It generally follows prompts well, and it feels less restricted in what you can ask it to do. But the quality needs work. It distorted my face quite a bit, and asking for edits to start at a specific moment was unreliable. Some happened too late, while others didn’t happen at all. title: 1 Prompt to 30-second Ad with Seedance 2.5  Prompt: Create a 30-secon...
description: 1 Prompt to 30-second Ad with Seedance 2.5  Prompt: Create a 30-second photorealistic 16:9 commercial for VYRA Sparkling Water, filmed like a serious action thriller. The characters never acknowledge the absurdity. Contemporary realistic world, ARRI Alexa 35 look, 24 fps, natural motion blur and realistic lighting. REFERENCES @ops leader; @scientist 1; @scientist 2; @waiter; @customer; @VYRA Bottle. Preserve each character’s identity, age, face, hair, body, clothing and accessories. Preserve @VYRA Bottle exactly: emerald-green glass, gold cap, ivory-and-gold label, condensation and readable VYRA branding. CONTINUITY There is only one ice cube and one case. The compact brushed-metal case has a black handle, three mechanical locks, dark insulated interior and small blue temperature display. Never duplicate or redesign either object. Show the case only when requested. [0–4 seconds] One continuous long-lens street shot presented as live TV news footage. A modern city avenue in an extreme heatwave: harsh midday sun, strong heat shimmer, slow traffic and a few exhausted pedestrians under umbrellas. Restrained overlay: “LIVE | CITY HEAT EMERGENCY.” A serious female newsreader, never shown, says immediately over the full shot: “As the heatwave continues, authorities have confirmed that only one ice cube remains.” No cuts or extra actions. [4–7 seconds] One slow push-in inside a secure refrigerated laboratory under cold white light, with frosted metal surfaces and low cold vapor. @scientist 1 and @scientist 2 stand beside a small transparent refrigerated container holding the single perfect ice cube. They stare at it with complete seriousness as the camera pushes toward the cube. [7–8 seconds] Macro close-up. @scientist 1 lifts the ice cube from the container with stainless-steel tongs. Keep the cube and tongs visible. [8–10 seconds] Close shot. @scientist 2 holds the case open while @scientist 1 places the cube inside. She closes the lid; all three locks engage and the blue display turns green. [10–12 seconds] At the laboratory exit, @scientist 2 hands the sealed case to @ops leader. @ops leader takes it by the handle and walks toward a waiting black security SUV. Keep her and the complete case visible. [12–14 seconds] Wide aerial shot. The SUV speeds along a sunlit avenue, two police motorcycles clearing the road and one helicopter following. @ops leader and the case remain inside and are not visible. Do not show the case. [14–16 seconds] The same SUV stops outside an elegant contemporary restaurant. The rear door opens and @ops leader exits holding the case by its handle. Keep her and the full case visible. [16–18 seconds] Inside, the camera tracks backward as @ops leader carries the case toward one table. Two guards follow; seated diners quietly turn to watch. She never releases or exchanges the case. [18–19 seconds] At the table, @customer is seated and @waiter stands ready. @ops leader places the sealed case flat on the table. [19–21 seconds] Macro close-up. @ops leader releases the three locks and opens the lid. Cold vapor reveals the single intact cube; the display remains stable. [21–22 seconds] @waiter lifts the cube from the open case with polished silver tongs while @ops leader holds the lid. [22–25 seconds] One continuous macro close-up of a crystal glass filled with clear VYRA sparkling water. @waiter lowers the cube into it. The tense music stops exactly as the cube enters. It hits the glass with one sharp clink, cracks slightly and triggers a rush of fine carbonation bubbles. The cube remains in the glass. Do not show the case. [25–27 seconds] Medium close-up. @customer lifts the glass, takes one slow sip, pauses and gives one small approving nod. @ops leader and @waiter watch silently in the background. No smiles, laughter, applause or exaggerated reactions. [27–30 seconds] Steady studio product shot of @VYRA Bottle beside the chilled glass containing the cube. Clear water and fine bubbles are visible through the green glass #seedance25

title: How well can Seedance 2.5 replicate motion from a 3D render? I tested...
description: How well can Seedance 2.5 replicate motion from a 3D render? I tested it with two very different scenes. The capoeira sequence tests whether it can preserve complex full-body choreography, including kicks, spins, floor movements, balance, and transitions between animations. The zombie run tests something else: a long continuous camera move, a moving main character, and an entire crowd of zombies spread throughout the scene. I built both scenes in Blender using Mixamo animations, rendered them as simple 3D blockouts, and used those videos as motion and camera references in Seedance 2.5. I also uploaded an image of myself so the model could rebuild the main character and turn everything into realistic live-action footage. It’s a really interesting way to control AI video. Instead of hoping the model invents the right movement and camera work from a text prompt, you can design both in 3D first. Which test do you think worked better: capoeira or the zombie run? #dreaminaseedance25 #seedance #blender# #3d #seedance25

title: HyperFrames Day 8 - Editing Talking Head Videos HyperFrames can analy...
description: HyperFrames Day 8 - Editing Talking Head Videos HyperFrames can analyze your talking-head footage and add synchronized captions, motion graphics, cards, music, and sound effects. You can let HyperFrames decide how to edit the video. But for more granular control, give it specific instructions for each spoken line. Here is the prompt I used: Use HyperFrames /talking-head-recut to edit my uploaded 1920×1080 horizontal talking-head video using the supplied transcript for exact word timing. Keep the original footage untouched. Do not trim it, split it, add jump cuts, rearrange it, or change its speed. Use the installed Particle Burst captions throughout. Keep captions at the bottom and place all other graphics above them. Add background music and synchronized sound effects across the full video. When I say, “Claude can now edit your entire talking-head video,” show a bright text box above my head reading “Claude Edited This Video.” When I say, “It automatically transcribes everything you say and adds these animated captions to your clip,” slide in a card from the right reading “Automatic Transcription & Captioning.” When I mention my social media stats, show three liquid-glass cards: TikTok: 130K Followers Instagram: 82K Followers Facebook: 115K Followers On “But that’s not all,” clear all graphics and leave only the captions. Then use a Cross Warp Morph transition. When I say, “It can move me to the side, split the screen, and use the other half for graphs, animations, or anything else that supports what I’m saying,” move me to the left and use the right half for an animated graph titled “BS LEVEL,” rising sharply to “MAXIMUM.” Then replace it with a loading bar that reaches 100% and bursts into a checkmark. Keep the checkmark visible until the sentence ends. When I say, “It can add lower thirds with a Follow call to action,” show a YouTube lower third using my supplied avatar: Victor C 6.8K Subscribers Include a Subscribe button that changes to Subscribed. When I say, “create liquid glass boxes for quotes,” raise a liquid-glass quote box reading: “Every word becomes a visual cue.” During “and time every element to the exact moment it is mentioned,” animate a timing line across the quote box and land it on a marker. When I mention background music and sound effects, show two cards reading “MUSIC” and “SFX,” then merge them into a “FINAL POLISH” card. During “so your raw footage turns into a fully edited, professional video,” transform “RAW FOOTAGE” into “FULLY EDITED.” Render the finished video. #hyperframes
